column1: # OWASP ZAP baseline scan rules for the DAST job (.github/workflows/dast.yml).
# Tab-separated: <alertId>
#   action = IGNORE  — accepted / not applicable, never fails the scan
#            WARN     — reported, does not fail the scan (default for anything not listed)
#            FAIL     — reported and fails the scan
#   url-regex — omit (empty 3rd column) to apply to every URL; otherwise a Python
#               regex matched against the finding's URL
# Posture: BLOCKING — both legs (fail-action: true, both check-runs required in the
# branch ruleset).
# alert IDs: https://www.zaproxy.org/docs/alerts/
# --- Triaged from the 2026-09-10 unauthenticated baseline of Wayfinder.Umbraco.ReferenceApp,
#     after the security-headers middleware (#74). ---
# Absence of Anti-CSRF Tokens — the demo login form only. A pre-auth login form has no
# session to protect with a synchroniser token; the citizen/caseworker POST forms behind
# auth carry __RequestVerificationToken. Verified by the Phase 3c authenticated scan: this
# finding did NOT reappear on any authenticated page — every caseworker POST genuinely
# carries the token, not just untested until now.
# CSP style-src 'unsafe-inline' — required on the Wayfinder-rendered front end: the two
# inline style="…" attributes on the signed-in nav in ReferenceAppPageShell.cs, plus
# Umbraco's Block Grid layout partials which emit inline style="--umb-block-grid-…" custom
# properties on every seeded page. script-src has NO 'unsafe-inline' and NO 'unsafe-eval'.

column4: inline style attrs (nav + Umbraco Block Grid custom properties)

column1: # Cross-Origin-* headers (COEP / COOP / CORP all report under 90004):
#   COEP — not adopted anywhere: it only matters for cross-origin isolation
#          (SharedArrayBuffer / high-res timers), which this host does not use.
#   COOP / CORP — present on the Wayfinder front end (set by the #74 middleware); absent
#          only on /umbraco*, which the middleware deliberately excludes (see below).

column4: COEP unused estate-wide; COOP/CORP set on the front end, /umbraco* excluded

column1: # ---- /umbraco* : the Umbraco backoffice owns its own header + CSP regime ----
# The reference app's security-headers middleware is deliberately scoped to skip /umbraco*
# (a Lit web-component SPA a strict CSP would break) — the same ExcludeBackoffice posture
# Umbraco.Prism's PrismSecurityHeadersOptions ships. A real deployment fronts the backoffice
# with its own policy (reverse proxy / WAF), and it is often not publicly reachable at all.
# Each line is path-scoped so the identical header regressing on the *front end* still fails.

column4: CSP: backoffice, Umbraco-owned (a strict CSP would break the backoffice SPA)
X-Content-Type-Options: backoffice + its static assets, Umbraco-owned

column1: # --- Triaged from the 2026-09-11 authenticated (Phase 3c) baseline, signed in as the demo
#     caseworker — 42 URLs reached vs. the unauthenticated scan's much smaller surface. ---
# User Controllable HTML Element Attribute (Potential XSS) — the worklist search box
# reflects ?q= back into its <input value="…">. Same shared Wayfinder.Engine.Worklist
# WorklistRenderer core's own Phase 3c pass already verified (see jonnymuir/Wayfinder's own
# .zap/rules.tsv): rendered via esc(q ?? "") → GovUk.Esc → WebUtility.HtmlEncode. ZAP's
# heuristic can't see server-side escaping, it just flags "user input landed in an
# attribute". Genuinely escaped, not a vulnerability.

column4: q is HTML-encoded via GovUk.Esc (WebUtility.HtmlEncode) before landing in value="…"
